entries.template: no operator is spelled '{op}'
entries.fix: the parser builds only the operators the language defines, so reaching this is a defect in the interpreter rather than in the program — worth reporting with the source

entries.fix: arithmetic is + - * /; reaching this means apply_op routed an operator here that it does not itself arithmetic on, which is a defect in the interpreter rather than in the program

entries.template:
line {lineno}: unrecognized escape '\{nxt}' in a string literal
  the four recognized escapes are \" \\ \n \t -- for any other character, write the character itself

line {lineno}: unterminated string literal -- no closing quote found before the end of the line
  add the closing quote; a Planes string cannot span multiple lines, so a long one has to be joined with + across lines

line {lineno}: unterminated string literal -- a backslash right before the closing quote escapes that quote (\") instead of ending the string
  the four recognized escapes are \" \\ \n \t -- write \\ for a literal trailing backslash
no module named '{name}'
entries.fix: create {name}.planes next to this file, or use one of: {', '.join(sorted(BUILTIN_MODULES))}
rename one at the point of use, e.g. `use {other_mod} with {first} as my {first}`
entries.note: message is not a literal/f-string at the call site (built elsewhere)

entries.template: module cycle: {cycle}
entries.fix: break the cycle by moving shared code to a third file

entries.template:
line {t.line}: expected an effect name after {after}, found '{t.value or 'end of line'}'
  valid kinds: {', '.join(sorted(EFFECT_KINDS))} — and 'nothing' after 'doing', for a foreign that performs none

line {g.line}: unrecognised entry in a note, found '{g.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: from "source"  or  derives-from [rule-name]

line {t.line}: expected a value, found '{t.value or 'end of line'}'
  a value starts with a number, a quoted string, true, false, nothing, a name, `not`, a list, a record, or a parenthesised expression — a statement word like `show` or `write` cannot stand in for one

entries.template: line {g.line}: expected {value or kind.lower()}, found '{found}'
entries.no_fix: this is the generic token gate, reached from every form in the grammar; it knows which token was due and not what the author meant by writing another, so a call site that can say more passes `fix=` and a call site that cannot says nothing rather than guessing

entries.template:
line {line}: '{name}' is a builtin, so it cannot be {what}
  builtin names are reserved like keywords; pick another name (a function definition may still shadow it with `to {name} ...:`)

line {g.line}: '{g.value}' is not a parameter of this function, so it cannot be where '{kind}' goes
  parameters: {', '.join(params) or 'none'}

line {g.line}: a rule needs a bracketed name, found '{g.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: rule [name-here] subject may not effect-kind

line {g.line}: a rule's bracketed name must be a word, found '{g.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: rule [name-here] subject may not effect-kind

line {kind_tok.line}: '{kind}' is not an effect kind a rule can name
  valid kinds: {', '.join(sorted(EFFECT_KINDS))}

line {g.line}: 'because' needs a quoted reason
  try: cap = 200 because "the reason"

line {t.line}: expected a field name, found '{t.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: with name: value

line {g.line}: '[' has no meaning here — Planes has no index or slice syntax
  try: first n of x — takes the first n code points or items; there is no way to take one position or a range

line {g.line}: expected a name, found '{g.value or 'end of line'}'
  a name here is one or more plain words — the old or the new spelling in a `use ... with <old> as <new>` rename; a quoted string, a number, or a punctuation mark cannot stand for one

line {t.line}: expected a field name, found '{t.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: { name: value }  or  { name }

line {tokens[i + 1].line}: '{tokens[i + 1].value}' is a reserved word and cannot start a function name
  reserved: {', '.join(sorted(KEYWORDS))}

line {tokens[j].line}: '{tokens[j].value}' is a reserved word and cannot appear in the function name '{' '.join(parts)} {tokens[j].value}'
  reserved: {', '.join(sorted(KEYWORDS))}

line {g.line}: '{found}' is a keyword, so it cannot be used as a name
  keyword names are reserved like builtins; pick another name

line {g.line}: expected {value or kind.lower()}, found '{found}'
  {fix}

line {g.line}: 'supersedes' needs a bracketed rule name, found '{g.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: {form} supersedes [other-rule-name]

line {g.line}: 'supersedes' needs a bracketed rule name, found '{g.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: {form} supersedes [other-rule-name]

line {g.line}: 'from' in a note needs a quoted source
  try: from "the source"

line {g.line}: 'derives-from' needs a bracketed rule name, found '{g.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: derives-from [rule-name]

line {g.line}: 'derives-from' needs a bracketed rule name, found '{g.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: derives-from [rule-name]

line {t.line}: expected a field name, found '{t.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: { name: value }

line {at_tok.line}: a fingerprint must be exactly six hex characters after '@', found '{bad.value or 'end of line'}'
  try: {form} supersedes [{supersedes}] @abcdef — or omit it for an unverified override

line {t.line}: field '{k}' appears twice in this record
  keep one of the two; to change a field's value later, build a new record from this one — `r with {k}: value`

rule [{rule.name}] (line {rule.line}): subject '{rule.subject}' does not resolve to anything in the traced effect surface — checking it needs a value this file's derivation graph can reach
  check the name is spelled as it appears in this file, or write the rule against 'anything' instead

rule [{rule.name}] (line {rule.line}): subject '{rule.subject}' only resolves in {other}, not in the file that declares this rule — a rule cannot reach across an import boundary to a name it never saw declared
  write the rule in {other} instead, or name a subject local to this file

two rules are both named [{r.name}] (line {other.line} and line {r.line}) — a rule name must be unique
  rename one of them

rule [{r.name}] (line {r.line}) supersedes itself
  supersedes should name an earlier, different rule

rule [{r.name}] (line {r.line}) supersedes [{r.supersedes}], which is not a rule in this file
  check the name, or remove the supersedes clause

rule [{p.name}] (line {p.line}) permits '{p.kind}' but excepts no forbid rule — a permit only has force against a prohibition it supersedes or narrows
  add 'supersedes [name-of-the-forbid-rule]' to [{p.name}], or give it a target that narrows one of the forbid rules over '{p.kind}'

rule [{a.name}] (line {a.line}) and rule [{b.name}] (line {b.line}) are equally specific over {where} — neither narrows nor supersedes the other
  add 'supersedes [{a.name}]' to [{b.name}] (or the reverse), or give one of them a target the other lacks

rule [{r.name}] (line {r.line}) supersedes [{r.supersedes}] (line {target_rule.line}) as of @{r.supersedes_fingerprint}, but [{r.supersedes}] is now @{actual} — it changed after [{r.name}] was written to override it
  confirm the override still means what it meant, then update the fingerprint to @{actual}

rule [{forbid.name}] (line {forbid.line}) and rule [{permit.name}] (line {permit.line}) demand opposite things over {where} — one forbids it, the other permits it, and neither narrows nor supersedes the other
  add 'supersedes [{forbid.name}]' to [{permit.name}] to make the exception explicit, or give one of them a target the other lacks
[{self.rule.name}] would have been violated at line {self.effect.site} — excepted by [{self.cleared_by.name}] (line {self.cleared_by.line})

[{rule.name}] (line {rule.line}) checked nothing — subject '{rule.subject}' resolves in this file, but the program performs no '{rule.kind}' effect at all
the rule is inert against this program as written
check the program still performs the effect you expect, or remove the rule if it no longer applies

[{rule.name}] (line {rule.line}) checked nothing — subject '{rule.subject}' derives a '{rule.kind}' effect, but the rule's target excludes every one
'{rule.subject}' reaches this effect kind, but never at "{escape_string_literal(rule.target)}"
check the target matches where '{rule.subject}' actually goes, or remove the target to check every '{rule.kind}' effect '{rule.subject}' reaches

[{rule.name}] (line {rule.line}) checked nothing — subject '{rule.subject}' resolves in this file, but no '{rule.kind}' effect derives from it
the program performs '{rule.kind}', but to a target that does not derive from '{rule.subject}'
check the subject names the value you meant, or write the rule against 'anything'
